newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: INSTANT VIEW-S.Korea's financial reform proposals.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW-S.Korea's financial reform proposals.

text.p: Following are comments by economists on financial reform proposals presented by a special commission to President Kim Young-sam on Tuesday:
LEE HAHN-KOO, PRESIDENT OF DAEWOO ECONOMIC RESEARCH INSTITUTE:
"The goal of the proposals is to promote competitiveness in the financial market. If they will be implemented as proposed, it will contribute to the economy."
"But the commission's draft was a huge-scale programme, which needs further deep study. If we hurry its implementation, it will cause a crisis, as the current financial market remains unstable."
"The proposals should have had more details on bank ownership and a future financial universal system."
JWA SEUNG-HEE, PRESIDENT OF KOREA INSTITUTE OF ECONOMY:

"I welcome the panel's proposal to give independence to the central bank to implement monetary policy consistently. But I question how the central bank's governor will be able to act independently when he will be appointed by the president. His employment should be approved by parliament."
"But I don't understand why unification of the supervisory boards should be speeded up. The commission provided no details on how the boards would be unified or any schedule for universal banking."
"The proposals should have given details about how the government would deal with a financial institution that wanted to expand to other financial business lines."

"I have no doubt the commission worked hard to prepare the proposals. But they seemed to be pressured to write their draft in a short time. The proposals included no study of how they impact the economy."

"People seemed to overlook the real important issues of bank ownership. Under current banking rules, the percentage of an individual's shareholding is of no significance. We need more concrete rules to let shareholders exercise their rights in board meetings, including appointing the president and setting bank policies."
LEE IN-HYUNG, RESEARCH DIRECTOR AT LG ECONOMIC RESEARCH INSTITUTE:
"By allowing more entrants into the financial industry, the proposals paved the way for a long-term industrial shake-out following hot competition."
"The strict criteria on bank ownership will eventually prevent chaebol from owning banks and make mergers and acquisitions more difficult for the time being."

"The independence of the central bank will not have a real impact on the economy, even though the issue is significant for the bank. By stressing the monetary authority of the central bank, the government is likely to put a priority on inflation."

"The unified supervisory board will weaken the authority of the finance ministry. But most of the board's new spots will be filled with former finance ministry officials, so it won't be much different."
"The overall direction was quite right, including provisions to improve competitiveness and deregulate. But the proposals dealt with too many issues and fell short on details."
"I doubt they will be implemented because the proposals have been prepared in haste by a lame-duck government."
PARK KYUNG-SUH, SENIOR ECONOMIST AT KOREA INSTITUTE OF FINANCE:

"Most of the proposals are indirect reforms of Korea's backward financial industry. The commission should have explained more how to remove business barriers among banks, insurers and securities houses."
"The unified supervisory board will be a big issue for relevant authorities. It will not affect any financial institutions, as they don't care who supervises them.
"The proposals fell short of anticipated Big Bang reforms."
-- SEOUL NEWSROOM (822) 727 5647
